report.summary: Shackleton rim lunar target: three Earth twins best match terrain and light, Peru leads. Four field tests proposed, with Earth-only limits listed.

claims.text: Low-sun navigation at the Peru twin, its best light match, during its 05-23 to 06-19 window.
Slope traverse at the Switzerland twin, close in mean slope and local relief to the target.
Shadowed-area operations at the China twin, whose 12 km roughness differs most from the target.
Comms relay drill timed to landing, when Earth sits low on the horizon at the target.

tests.name: Low-sun slope traverse
tests.why: Switzerland is close in mean slope and local relief, and has the best light match.

tests.name: Low-sun navigation
tests.why: Peru has the highest score and the closest topographic position; light caveat limits it to terrain-led navigation.

tests.name: Shadowed-area operations
tests.why: Rough terrain and December low sun approximate target shadow-handling; the site-finder shows small shadowed areas.

tests.why: Earth sits low on the horizon at landing, so relay pointing and line-of-sight margins need rehearsal.

disagreements.about: Mars twin has the best terrain similarity; light favours Switzerland.

disagreements.about: Peru ranks first on score; light specialist distrusts its high-sun profile.
disagreements.resolution: Peru kept as secondary, for terrain-led tests only. Switzerland is the primary site.

disagreements.about: China is a modest terrain match but is proposed for shadowed-area tests.
disagreements.resolution: Kept for rough-terrain procedure rehearsal only; it does not reproduce permanently shadowed conditions.

Vacuum conditions cannot be replicated in ordinary test sites

limitations: Sunlight uses an analytic model: circular orbit, no eccentricity, no local horizon or terrain shadowing.
Similarity is terrain shape only (slope, roughness, relief, curvature); not geology, chemistry or regolith.
Terrain is compared at one common ground scale; features smaller than the grid spacing are not seen.
Environment data (country, climate, airport) is a coarse proxy for logistics; no routing or permits checked.
Similarity covers terrain shape and analytic light only, not geology, chemistry or regolith.
Light model has no local horizon or terrain shadowing; low-sun matches are approximate.
No country, climate, elevation or airport context data for any candidate site.
